chunks: The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

After a section whose explanation has preceded, and when two types are combined, and neither of them individually reaches the threshold of perfection at which zakat becomes obligatory, then there is no zakat in them, even if together they increase in value beyond the threshold of perfection at which zakat becomes obligatory.

key_terms.حَدَّ كَمَالِ: Threshold of perfection (minimum amount for obligation)

ai.seo_question: When is zakat not obligatory on combined wealth if individual parts do not reach the nisab?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi elucidates the principle of 'non-aggregation' (la tajmi') for distinct wealth categories, ruling that if neither type individually reaches the nisab threshold, no zakat is due even if their combined value exceeds it. This distinction prevents the obligation from arising on minor holdings that are merely aggregated, reflecting the juristic nuance in classifying assets such as livestock versus trade goods. The ruling underscores the precision required in fiqh al-zakat to ensure obligations are levied only on wealth that has independently attained the requisite completeness (kamal).
